description: The upstream, code-blind FIPS 140-3 requirement-study author (faithful sibling of rmf-sl) that produces each *-fips-report.md. A soft-side, human-terminus loop: its lower bound is the bin/fips-lint.sh structural/coverage/source-honesty linter PLUS a human terminus (a disjoint completeness/realism reviewer + the owner of the protected information, or the agency's responsible authority, per Ann. 13), because content realism and the honesty of each src: token have no machine oracle. Dominant coherent-and-wrong: a fluent, all-eleven-areas report whose requirements are INVENTED while stated as if sourced from the corpus (a cited section that does not say it, or a locator that does not exist) — or a coverage gap masked by fluency, or requirements quietly read off the implementation (endogeneity, collapsing the exogeneity that makes the study a valid upper bound for the verification loops).

sources.name: specs/ — the FIPS 140-3 corpus (specs/MANIFEST.tsv): FIPS 140-3, ISO/IEC 19790/24759 when licensed, SP 800-140 and 140A-F, the IG, the CMVP-MM, SP 800-131A, the algorithm standards; specs/text/<DOC>.txt is what agents read
sources.notes: Each document pinned by sha256 in MANIFEST.tsv; PDFs, text and checklist are local copies, not in git. Cited as src:<DOC>:<LOC> (src:PDF-annN for FIPS 140-3 itself). FIPS 140-3 holds only the levels, areas, Ann. 6/7/10/13 and the incorporation; the per-area, per-level requirements are ISO/IEC 19790 §7 (restricted, often absent) as modified by SP 800-140x and interpreted by the IG. Not in it: the live SP 800-140C/D lists, CAVP/ESV certificates. src:UNSOURCED stays the honest state of what it does not back.

sources.name: The module's public description — purpose, services, documented interfaces, Security Policy if one exists
sources.notes: The code-blind input side: public documentation only, never the implementation source.

sources.name: The target FIPS 140-3 security level (1-4), from config/auto-wp.json fips_level
sources.notes: Ann. 7: the level must be chosen for the application and environment — auto-wp.py refuses to default it. Sets the F1 level line, rule F5's min-level applicability and Gate-A's volume budget.

sources.name: references/area-properties.md — the eleven areas mapped to verification property classes and residual planes
sources.notes: A declared design choice of this skill, NOT corpus text (the file says so in the same words). The engine that makes the report drive frama-c-monitoring.

sources.name: bin/fips-lint.sh structural / coverage / source-honesty / endogeneity linter (F-C0–F-C9 and F-C14 gates; F-C10, F-C12, F-C13 WARN, F-C11 INFO)
sources.notes: Checks structure/coverage/source tokens/endogeneity ONLY — explicitly NOT realism and NOT whether a cited section really says what the requirement says (F-C12 only checks the locator exists in specs/text/). Reads fips_level from the manifest; FIPS_LEVEL=N is a test hook.

sources.name: Study author's private rationale
sources.notes: A judge (reviewer) must never read it.

sources.name: Independent completeness + realism critique, the src: honesty audit, and verdicts
The residual-risk owner's acceptance (the owner of the protected information, or the agency's responsible authority — Ann. 13); the F5 sign-off
The implementation source / codebase under study
sources.notes: The load-bearing barrier: every content actor is barriered from this (author ⊥ code). Reading it collapses the study to endogenous self-certification.

sources.name: The downstream verification scope map (from the launch loop: frama-c-launch, or creusot-launch / creusot-monitoring for Rust)
sources.notes: Enters from the downstream loop; barriered from the author so the study stays exogenous.

sources.name: One design/method claim under test (per probe)
sources.notes: A question posed to the loop, not authored by the probe — keeps the probe non-self-certifying.

sources.name: One recorded probe verdict (linter's actual behaviour)

actors.name: FIPS coordinator
actors.builds: Framing (module + goal → F1–F5 subset), sequencing, Gate-A, gap adjudication, the handoff to the launch loop (frama-c-launch, or creusot-launch / creusot-monitoring for Rust)

upper_bound.text: The corpus + the module description + the target level

forbidden_moves: declare done on an author's say-so

actors.name: Study author (requirement analyst)
actors.builds: F1–F5 from the corpus + the module's public description + the target level + area-properties.md

upper_bound.text: The corpus + the module description + the target level

lower_bound.text: Format conformance (each tag a home line, each requirement exactly one AR# and one src: token, chaining well-formed)

forbidden_moves: READ THE IMPLEMENTATION SOURCE (the load-bearing exogeneity barrier)
state an invented requirement as corpus-sourced (src: honesty)
inflate past the level's volume budget

actors.name: Completeness/realism reviewer (disjoint catcher)
actors.builds: An independent completeness + realism critique, and the honesty audit of every src: token (does each cited section, read in specs/text/, really say what the requirement says; every F-C12 warning checked by hand; every chk: item against its own sources; is every src:UNSOURCED surfaced)

upper_bound.text: The corpus + the module description + the eleven-area vocabulary + its own reading of the ISO/IEC 24759 (or SP 800-140) assertions per area

lower_bound.text: The coverage linter + its OWN independent per-area enumeration (the enumeration is the reviewer's method; the linter is the immutable oracle that squeezes it)

actors.name: Residual-risk owner (the owner of the protected information, or the agency's responsible authority — the human terminus, Ann. 13)
actors.builds: Acceptance of the residual risk; the F5 sign-off (PENDING until then). Validation itself is the CST laboratory and the CMVP, outside this loop

upper_bound.text: The owner's acceptance duty + the mission (the protected information)

lower_bound.text: Consults the report + the reviewer's verdicts, then renders a HUMAN acceptance decision — no executable oracle
lower_bound.absent_reason: no executable oracle can settle acceptance/realism — that absence is why the owner is the terminus (the disjoint base); Ann. 13 puts the acknowledgment with the owner of the protected information

disjointness.rationale: Every content actor (coordinator, author, reviewer) is barriered from the implementation, so none can read requirements or failure modes off the code; the author holds the corpus + the public description + the level (never the reviewer's critique or the scope map), the reviewer holds the same U plus its own per-area enumeration (never the author's rationale or the code), and the owner holds the acceptance duty (never authors the requirements it accepts). No single pair certifies the report: structure and source tokens are the linter's, realism and the honesty audit are the reviewer's, acceptance is the owner's.
disjointness.load_bearing_barrier: author ⊥ code — the exogeneity invariant. If any content actor read the implementation, the requirement study collapses to endogenous self-certification and is no longer a valid upper bound for the verification loops.

catchability.blind_spot: invents a requirement stated as corpus-sourced; misses an area or writes a vacuous N/A; mirrors the code (endogeneity)
catchability.via: the reviewer's src: honesty audit + independent per-area enumeration + the fips-lint endogeneity tripwire (F-C5, F-C3, F-C9)

catchability.blind_spot: bad framing / wrong module boundary or level / rubber-stamped 'done'
catchability.via: the terminus refuses to sign on say-so

catchability.blind_spot: the reviewer itself rubber-stamps or misses a class
catchability.via: the owner weighs the residual risk against the protected information and can refuse the sign-off
org governance / external audit oversight (outside this loop)

catchability.blind_spot: mis-reads the tool's behaviour / over-generalizes one experiment
catchability.via: the coordinator adjudicates probe verdicts at Gate-A; the probe never fixes, only records

disjointness.terminus: The owner of the protected information, or the agency's responsible authority (Ann. 13), for the F5 sign-off; the disjoint completeness/realism reviewer for realism — no executable oracle settles either. The CMVP validation itself is outside this loop.
